Bug_Details:
Scope annotation on implementation class of AssistedInject factory is not allowed Classes that AssistedInject factories create may not be annotated with scope
annotations, such as @Singleton. This will cause a Guice error at runtime. See
this bug report
for details.
Bug_Explanation: This code demonstrates the 'GuiceAssistedInjectScoping' bug. The bug occurs when a class created by a Guice AssistedInject factory is annotated with a scope annotation. The class 'MyClass' is annotated with '@Singleton', but it is created by a factory. This will cause a Guice error at runtime.

Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggers the bug by calling the'showBug' method of 'BugDemo' class. This method in turn creates an instance of 'MyClass' using the 'Factory' class which doesn't adhere to the GuiceAssistedInjectScoping rule. The 'MyClass' is annotated with @Singleton which is not allowed for classes created by AssistedInject factories. This will cause a Guice error at runtime.
Model_Explanation: The described bug is not present in the provided Java code. The @Singleton annotation is used on the MyClass class, which is a valid use of the @Singleton annotation. This annotation is used to indicate that a single instance of the class should be created and shared among all users of the class.
